te: Helping SMEs reach the government market transparently: ways to prevent corruption in public procurement
se: Meeting on Thursday 19 November 2026 at 13.00, Committee Meeting Room CB 311 (Senate), Floor 3, Parliament House, according to the meeting notice: the agenda is to consider ways to prevent corruption in public procurement and subcontracting, and to promote good governance and fair competition, so that SMEs have a better chance to reach the government market in a transparent and sustainable way. The summary will be added once the Senate publishes it.
it: Ways to prevent corruption in public procurement and subcontracting, and to promote good governance and fair competition, so that SMEs have a better chance to reach the government market in a transparent and sustainable way

te: Pre-meeting video · Helping SMEs reach the government market transparently: ways to prevent corruption in public procurement
Hearing ways to prevent corruption in public procurement, so SMEs get a fair chance
se: The subcommittee invited representatives of the Anti-Corruption Organization of Thailand to give information. The representatives said that existing tools, such as the Integrity Pact and the CoST project, have improved transparency to some degree, but that gaps remain, such as bidder qualifications that limit competition, the use of scoring systems, splitting contracts into amounts below the thresholds, and sub-contracting through several layers, which make it hard for SMEs to win government work. The recommendations received were: disclosing the true shareholders of government suppliers, automatic blacklisting of contractors who abandon work, checking suppliers' readiness before they may bid, making the e-GP and e-Marketplace systems easier to use, and linking tax data so that SMEs are warned in advance. The subcommittee chair thanked the representatives for kindly giving information, and the subcommittee will use the information and recommendations in preparing its study report.
it: Information from representatives of the Anti-Corruption Organization of Thailand on tools for preventing corruption in public procurement, and the gaps that should be improved

Recommendations: disclose true shareholders, blacklist contractors who abandon work automatically, check suppliers' readiness, improve the e-GP and e-Marketplace systems, and link tax data to warn SMEs
